body.heading: Where in the world is Italy?
paragraphs: Italy is a country in Southern Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Italy is Rome.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Italy is Italian.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Italy is the euro. The euro is shared by many countries in Europe, so the same coins and notes work across borders.

body.heading: How big is Italy?
paragraphs: Italy covers about 301,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Ukraine.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: Venice is built on islands linked by bridges and canals. Venice has no roads for cars at all — its streets are water, and its buses and taxis are boats.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Rome is an open-air museum: the Colosseum where gladiators fought, the Forum's ruins, the Pantheon's dome and gelato on every corner.
Venice floats on water — gondolas and vaporettos instead of cars, St Mark's Square with its campanile, and bridges at every turn.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Italy on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Italy in one breath: a country in Southern Europe, capital Rome, where people speak Italian and pay with the euro.
